newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes to support won.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in early Thursday trading, offering to sell dollars at 917.00 won in six-month forward trading, and 939.00 in one-year forward trading, dealers said.
Dealers said the central bank's offers to sell $30 million each were immediately absorbed.
Central bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
Dealers said the bank later offered to sell another $30 million each in six-month and one-year forward trading, at similar rates.
In the spot trading, the won traded at 891.50 to the dollar, down from the day's opening of 890.00. It closed on Wednesday at 889.70.
Dealers said the local currency has been under pressure from the nation's rising trade deficit and the U.S. unit's strength versus the Japanese yen on overseas markets.
